error.api: The backend API is not reachable.
top.probeHint: Click on the slice plane to read exact field values (key P)
top.advancedHint: All parameters, solver details and numerical diagnostics
presets.title: Presets
preset.unavailable: Not available yet: no implemented solver supports this configuration (planned for phase {phase}).
objects.title: Objects
objects.addGeometry: Add inert geometry (not part of the physical model):
objects.inertHint: Inert geometry is drawn for reference only. It has no effect on the computed fields; physical roles for extended bodies are not supported yet.
objects.empty: The scene is empty. Add a charge or choose a preset.
params.nothingSelected: Select an object to edit its parameters.
params.name: Name
params.roleHint: Roles that no implemented solver supports are listed but cannot be selected.
params.inertNote: This object is inert geometry: it is drawn, but it is not part of the physical model and does not change the field.
params.chargeHint: Charge q in coulombs (shown in nC). The field direction follows the positive test-charge convention.
params.rotationNote: Rotation uses intrinsic XYZ Euler angles (R = Rx·Ry·Rz). Rotating or scaling an ideal point charge does not change its field.
params.domainHint: Bounds of the sampled and displayed region. The analytical model itself is unbounded.
viz.arrowsHint: Each arrow shows the direction of the field at its centre point; colour encodes its magnitude. Arrows are samples of the vector field, not field lines and not particle paths.
viz.arrowLengthHint: Visualization choice only; the computed field is not affected.
accuracy.title: Accuracy and cost
accuracy.explain: The field values are exact at every sample point; quality changes how densely the field is sampled and how tightly field lines are integrated. Preview ({preview} samples along the slice) is used while dragging, normal ({normal}) otherwise. A high-resolution solve ({high}) runs as a cancellable job on the solver worker and costs about 16× more.
accuracy.workerOffline: No solver worker is online, so queued jobs are unavailable. Interactive solving still works.
eq.intro: Every equation is shown with its status for the current physical model, and with whether the solver evaluates it directly or the computed field merely satisfies it. Click an equation for its meaning, symbols and assumptions.
eq.introBeginner: These equations describe the current scene. Click one to see what it means. Switch to Advanced to also see the equations that do not apply here, and why.
eq.status.not_applicable: Not applicable to the current model
eq.status.not_evaluated: Not evaluated by the current solver
results.noApproximation: No result is shown: an unsupported configuration is never replaced by a simpler, inaccurate model.
probe.title: Field probe
probe.enableHint: Choose the Probe tool, then click on the slice plane.
probe.clickHint: Click on the slice plane to place the probe.
probe.undefined: The probe is exactly on a point charge (within the position tolerance of {tol} m), where the field and the potential are singular and undefined.
probe.exactNote: Evaluated by the solver at this exact point in 64-bit precision (not interpolated from the displayed grid).
diag.note: Ranges are computed in 64-bit precision before the 32-bit transport cast; vector entries give the magnitude. The analytical solution has no discretization error; the only numerical error is floating-point rounding.
projects.title: Projects
projects.name: Project name
view.crossSection: Plane {where} through the full 3D configuration (not a two-dimensional model; nothing is assumed invariant along the normal). Arrows and field lines are 3D objects seen along the plane normal.
view.controls2d: Drag a charge to move it · right-drag: pan · wheel: zoom
view.3d: Full 3D model, z up. Slice plane at {where}.
view.controls3d: Drag: orbit · right-drag: pan · wheel: zoom · select an object to use the gizmo
legend.aidLog: Arrow length follows the log of the magnitude.
legend.aid: Colour ranges span the 2nd–98th percentile and are clamped beyond; charge markers have no physical size.
role.group: Group (container, no physical effect of its own)
objects.addDipoleHint: Adds two point charges +q and −q a distance d apart, grouped so they can be edited together. This is a physical pair of charges, not an ideal point dipole.
dipole.title: Dipole
dipole.momentHint: p = q·d, pointing from the negative to the positive charge.
dipole.note: The field is computed from the two point charges themselves (exact for any d). The ideal point-dipole limit d → 0 is not used.
dipole.unbalanced: The two charges are no longer equal and opposite.
dipole.broken: This group no longer contains exactly one positive and one negative point charge, so it cannot be edited as a dipole. Edit the charges individually.
params.flipHint: Change the sign of the charge, keeping its magnitude
viz.vectorFieldHint: E and D are different quantities with different units. In vacuum D = ε₀E, so the directions coincide.
viz.fieldLinesHint2d: Field lines are curves tangent to E everywhere; arrowheads show the direction of E (from + to −). They are not particle paths. In this cross-section the spacing of lines does not indicate field strength — use the colour map of |E|.
viz.fieldLinesHint3d: Field lines are curves tangent to E everywhere; arrowheads show the direction of E (from + to −). They are not particle paths. In 3D the number of lines leaving a charge is proportional to |q|, so line density roughly follows |E|.
viz.equipotentialsHint: On an equipotential φ is constant; E is perpendicular to it everywhere. Levels form a geometric ladder (each twice the previous), so they are not equally spaced in volts.
derived.title: Derived visualizations
derived.intro: These are computed numerically from the exact field. Their numerical method does not make the field itself approximate.
derived.noLines: No field lines: there is no charge to start them in this view.
derived.leavePlane: Not all charges lie in the slice plane, so these field lines are 3D curves that leave it. They are shown as seen along the plane normal and may appear to cross.
end.domain_boundary: edge of the region (line continues outside)
probe.superpositionNote: E is the vector sum of the Eᵢ and φ the plain sum of the φᵢ. The magnitudes |Eᵢ| do not simply add.
legend.numericalEnd: Line ended for a numerical reason
source.ghost: not in this slice: drawn at its projection; it is no singularity of the slice
viz.curlHint: The curl is a vector at every sample. For this electrostatic field it is exactly the zero vector everywhere the field is defined, so each sample shows a small ring (a zero vector has no direction) instead of an arrow. The field itself is not zero: compare with the field vectors.
viz.sourcesHint: Each charge is a delta source of divergence: ∇·E = Σ (qᵢ/ε₀) δ³(r − rᵢ). A delta has no finite value, so it is shown as a marker with its weight, not as a peak in a colour map. In 2D, charges that do not lie in the slice are drawn hollow at their projection, with their distance from the slice.
viz.divergenceHint: Divergence is a scalar: the net outward flux per unit volume. Choose ∇·E or ∇·D as the slice colour map: away from the charges it is exactly 0, although E is not.
viz.volumeScalarsHint: Shows the selected colour-map quantity as small cubes at the 3D sample points.
legend.divNote: Not a sampled spike: each charge's δ³ contribution is shown by its source marker, with its weight.
legend.curlNote: Magnitude of the curl vector. Zero curl means no rotation; the field itself is not zero.
legend.sources2d: Point sources (δ³ in ∇·E). Hollow: off this slice, shown at its projection.
legend.sources3d: Point sources (δ³ in ∇·E) at their true positions.
probe.notEvaluated: not evaluated (the field is undefined here)
probe.calculusNote: Exact analytical values: away from the charges every Coulomb term has zero divergence and zero curl, so these are exactly 0, while E is not.
probe.calculusSingularNote: At a charge the field has no classical value, so its pointwise divergence and curl are not evaluated. The distributional statement below applies instead.
probe.distExplain: The charge contributes a Dirac delta to the divergence with the weight shown; a delta has no finite value at this point, only its integral over a volume is a number. The curl stays zero in the distributional sense here too: a point charge is a source of divergence, never of rotation.
probe.atCharge: Place probe on the selected charge
probe.diagNote: Central differences of the exact field (step h = {h} m and h/2, Richardson-extrapolated), shown with an uncertainty bound. This is a check of the exact result above, not a replacement for it: a tiny nonzero estimate is round-off, not physics.
sources.title: Distributional sources
sources.intro: ρ = Σ qᵢ δ³(r − rᵢ), so ∇·E = Σ (qᵢ/ε₀) δ³(r − rᵢ) and ∇·D = Σ qᵢ δ³(r − rᵢ). Integrating over a volume gives Q_enc/ε₀ and Q_enc.
sources.curl: No source has a rotational weight: ∇×E = 0 and ∇×D = 0 hold everywhere, the charge positions included (distributionally).
cells.title: Subdivision {n}
cells.ambiguousNote: {names} lies on an internal cell boundary: it belongs to no single cell, so the per-cell volume integrals are not summed. The parent volume integral is unaffected.
cells.maxSharedSum: Largest |Φ_A + Φ_B| on a shared face
cells.note: Each internal face is used twice, once by each neighbour with opposite orientation, built from the same triangles: the two contributions cancel, so only the outer boundary remains.
explain.boundary: {n} charge(s) lie exactly on the surface. The field is singular there, so the flux is undefined: such a charge is neither inside nor outside. Move it off the surface to continue.
explain.enclosed: This surface encloses {npos} positive and {nneg} negative charge(s): Q_enc = {q}.
explain.flux: The surface integral gives Φ_E = {phi}; the volume integral of the divergence, computed separately from the enclosed δ³ sources, gives {vol}. They agree, as Gauss's law and the divergence theorem require.
explain.fluxInward: The normals point inward, so the surface integral is Φ_E = {phi}, the negative of the outward flux; the volume integral is {vol}.
explain.cancel: The enclosed charges cancel, so the net flux is zero, although flux leaves near the positive and enters near the negative charges.
explain.external: {n} external charge(s) change the field on the surface (entering and leaving patches), but their total contribution is {net} — zero up to round-off.
explain.near: {names} is close to the surface: the local flux density nearby is large, but the classification and the total are unchanged.
explain.empty: There are no charges: the field and the flux are zero.
explain.local: |E|, E·n and Φ_E are different quantities: a strong field running along the surface has a large |E| but little E·n, and contributes little flux.
flux.title: Flux through the Gaussian surface
flux.previewNote: Provisional result on the coarse preview mesh while something is being moved; the final result follows when you stop.
flux.invalid: This surface is not a valid closed surface; no flux is computed.
flux.ambiguous: A charge lies on this surface. The field is singular there, so the flux and the enclosed charge are undefined for this configuration.
flux.surfaceHint: Sum over all triangles and charges of q/(4πε₀) × signed solid angle: exact for the represented triangulated surface.
flux.volumeHint: Sum of the δ³ weights qᵢ/ε₀ of the charges strictly inside, found by a separate inside test (distance + ray casting).
flux.compareNote: The surface integral and the volume integral are computed by independent methods; their agreement is Gauss's law and the Gauss–Ostrogradsky theorem.
flux.compareNoteInward: With inward normals the surface integral is the negative of the outward flux, so it is compared with −∫ ∇·E dV.
flux.meshExact: The {shape} is represented exactly by flat triangles.
flux.meshApprox: A triangulated (inscribed) approximation of the ideal {shape}. This mesh is the integration surface: it is drawn, it decides inside/outside, and the flux is integrated over it.
flux.deviation: Largest deviation from the ideal shape
flux.geometryVsIntegration: Two different errors: the mesh deviates from the ideal shape (geometry, above), but the flux over the mesh is exact up to floating point (uncertainty in the table). Only a charge between the mesh and the ideal surface would be classified differently.
flux.idealDisagree: {names} lies between the mesh and the ideal surface: the ideal shape would classify it differently. The result follows the represented mesh.
flux.chargesNote: Signed distance: negative inside, positive outside. Each external charge's contribution Φ_E,i is zero up to round-off, although it changes the local flux density.
patch.title: Selected patch: triangle {n}
patch.perCharge: Contribution of each charge to this patch
patch.note: E·n and D·n are point samples at the centroid; Φ_E,T is the exact integral over the whole triangle (solid angle). They are different quantities.
gauss.title: Gaussian surfaces
gauss.intro: Imaginary closed surfaces for integrating flux. They are mathematical surfaces, not conductors or material boundaries, and do not change the field.
gauss.none: No Gaussian surface yet. Add one, or start a guided situation below.
gauss.cylinderAxis: The cylinder axis is the local z axis; rotate the surface to orient it.
gauss.customMesh: Custom mesh: dimensions are defined by its vertices.
gauss.reverseHint: Reversing all normals reverses the sign of every flux value: Φ → −Φ. The enclosed charge does not change.
gauss.subdivisionHint: In 3D the selected cell shows the flux through each of its faces; on internal faces the neighbour's contribution is equal and opposite.
gauss.colorByFlux: Colour by local flux density E·n
gauss.patchHint: In 3D, click the selected surface to inspect a triangle (patch).
gauss.situationsIntro: Each loads charges and surfaces; the explanation above updates as you change them.
gauss.twoD: In 2D: the surface's cross-section with the slice; flux values are 3D surface integrals.
legend.gaussTitle: Gaussian surfaces (local flux density at triangle centroids)
legend.gauss2d: 2D: lines are where the 3D surfaces cross this slice. Φ values below are full 3D surface integrals.
wire.infiniteNote: The wire is infinitely long and has zero radius; the drawn segment is only a picture of it, so it has no length to edit.
params.currentHintWire: Steady current in amperes. Positive current flows along the wire's direction vector.
params.currentHintLoop: Steady current in amperes. Positive current circulates counter-clockwise seen from the tip of the normal (right-hand rule).
params.reverseHint: Change the sign of the current. B and H reverse everywhere.
params.wireDirectionNote: The wire is the infinite line through the position, along the direction vector. Right-hand rule: thumb along the current, fingers curl along B.
params.loopDirectionNote: The loop lies in the plane perpendicular to its normal. With positive current, B on the axis points along the normal (right-hand rule).
params.resetHint: Restore this source's position, orientation, size and current from the loaded preset.
objects.addWireHint: Add an infinitely long straight wire carrying 10 A along z (current source).
objects.addLoopHint: Add a circular current loop of radius 0.5 m carrying 10 A (current source).
accuracy.bothFields: The scene has charges and currents: the high-resolution solve queues one job for the electric and one for the magnetic field.
legend.mAllNote: Each source's own field in its colour, at the same points: where the arrows point the same way the fields reinforce, where they point opposite ways they oppose. Lengths on a shared log scale.
legend.bLines: B field lines: {closed} closed, {truncated} truncated by the region (they continue outside; B lines have no ends)
legend.bNumerical: {n} line(s) ended numerically (not a physical end)
legend.currentSymbols: ⊙ current out of the screen, ⊗ into the screen. Right-hand rule: thumb along the current, fingers along B.
legend.bh: B in T and H in A/m are different quantities (B = μ₀H in vacuum); E and B never share a scale.
viz.fieldsShownHint: The electric and the magnetic field are separate quantities with separate scales and legends; they are never added together.
viz.magneticFieldHint: B (flux density, T) or H (field strength, A/m). In vacuum H = B/μ₀: same directions, different quantity and unit.
viz.contributionHint: Total field, the field of one source alone, or every source's own field side by side. All are computed by the engine; switching does not re-solve.
viz.bLinesHint: Integral curves of B. They have no start or end: a line is closed, or it is cut off by the edge of the region. Lines ending for numerical reasons are dashed.
viz.currentsHint: Wires are infinite: the drawn segment ends at ∞ marks only. Chevrons and ⊙/⊗ show the direction of positive current flow.
legend.divBNote: ∇·B = 0 does not mean B = 0. Current filaments are not magnetic monopoles: there is no magnetic source anywhere, and on the filaments only the distributional statement ∇·B = 0 applies.
probe.atCurrent: Place probe on the selected wire or loop
probe.magneticFields: Magnetic field values at the probe
probe.mSingularWire: The probe lies on the axis of wire {name} ({i}).
probe.mSingularLoop: The probe lies on a current filament of {name} ({i} per turn).
probe.mSingularExplain: An ideal filament has zero thickness, so B and H grow like 1/distance and have no pointwise value on it. A point counts as on the filament only when float64 cannot tell it apart from it (the tolerance scales with the source, about 1e-14 of its size); every other point, however close, gets its true field. A real wire has a finite radius and a finite field inside, which is outside this model.
probe.mDivNote: ∇·B and ∇·H are exactly zero here (analytical identity), although B is not zero.
probe.mDivSingularNote: On the filament only the distributional statement ∇·B = 0 holds; there is no pointwise value.
probe.mSuperpositionNote: B = Σ Bᵢ and H = Σ Hᵢ: each row is one source alone; the vector sum is the total above.
derived.magneticTitle: How the magnetic visualizations are made
derived.noBLines: No magnetic field lines in this view: no current source crosses the slice in a way that seeds them (for example a wire lying in the slice, whose B is perpendicular to it). Switch to 3D or another slice.
coil.lengthHint: Distance between the first and the last turn. With a single turn it is not used.
coil.singleTurn: N = 1: a single circular turn at the centre; the winding length is not used.
coil.spacingHint: Derived: Δz = L/(N−1). Turn positions are not set individually.
coil.idealNote: Valid only well inside a long, densely wound coil. The field shown in the view is the finite coil's, never this value.
coil.modelNote: Model: N separate circular turns, each an ideal filament; the field is their exact superposition (no helix pitch, no wire thickness).
torus.majorHint: Distance from the toroid's axis to the centre of the winding cross-section.
torus.windingHint: Radius of each circular turn (finite-turn model).
torus.coreHint: Radius of the circular core cross-section (ideal continuous-winding model).
torus.innerGap: Turn gap at the inner edge
torus.innerGapHint: Arc length 2π(R − b)/N between neighbouring turns where they are closest (geometry).
torus.invalid: Invalid geometry: the major radius must be larger than the winding or core radius.
torus.closeTurns: The turns are very close together at the inner edge; the field near them changes on a very small scale.
torus.usedFinite: The finite-turn model uses R, b and N; the core radius is kept for the ideal model.
torus.usedIdeal: The ideal model uses R, the core radius and N; the winding radius is kept for the finite model.
torus.modelHint: Finite-turn: N discrete circular turns in vacuum, field by superposition. Ideal: continuous winding on a linear core, H = NI/(2πρ) inside, zero outside.
torus.murHint: Linear, uniform core: B = μ₀μᵣH inside the core. H does not depend on μᵣ.
torus.idealNote: Idealization: the field is confined to the core and is exactly zero outside. It cannot be combined with other sources.
torus.finiteNote: The field outside the winding is computed, not assumed to be zero: it is small but not zero.
magnet.title: Magnetization
magnet.MHint: Uniform magnetization along the cylinder axis, in A/m. Its field comes from the bound surface current K = M × n on the side wall.
magnet.BrHint: Another way to enter M: B_r = μ₀M. A parameterization, not a material B–H curve.
magnet.reverseHint: Change the sign of M: north and south swap, B and H reverse everywhere.
magnet.note: Rigid, ideal magnetization: M does not change in response to other fields (no demagnetization, no hysteresis). A magnet carries no free current.
params.currentHintTurns: Current in every turn, in amperes. Positive current circulates counter-clockwise seen from the tip of the axis (right-hand rule).
params.solenoidDirectionNote: The coil's axis runs from the first to the last turn. With positive current, B inside points along the axis (right-hand rule).
params.toroidDirectionNote: The axis is the toroid's symmetry axis. With positive current, B circulates counter-clockwise about it inside the winding.
objects.addSolenoidHint: Add a finite solenoid: 20 circular turns of radius 0.04 m over 0.2 m, 1 A per turn.
objects.addToroidHint: Add a toroid of major radius 0.12 m with 24 turns of radius 0.03 m, 1 A per turn (finite-turn model).
objects.addMagnetHint: Add a uniformly magnetized cylinder (a = 0.04 m, L = 0.08 m, M = 5×10⁵ A/m along its axis).
ampere.title: Ampère's circuital law
ampere.intro: A closed planar path tests ∮H·dl = I_free,enclosed. The circulation is integrated numerically along the exact path; the enclosed free current is counted independently from where the currents cross the flat surface spanned by the path. Paths are mathematical, not physical objects.
ampere.none: No Ampère path yet. Add one above.
ampere.polygonHint: Vertices in the path's own plane (local x, y), in traversal order. The path must be closed, planar and must not cross itself.
ampere.orientationHint: Traversal direction. The positive surface normal follows the right-hand rule: curl the fingers along the path, the thumb gives n̂. Currents along n̂ count positive.
ampere.rtolHint: Target relative accuracy of the numerical circulation (with an absolute floor of 10⁻⁸ A scaled by the scene's currents). Smaller values take longer.
ampere.nearSingular: The path passes within {d} of a current filament: the integrand is sharply peaked there, the quadrature refines locally.
ampere.crossesMaterial: The path passes through magnetized material or the ideal core; it is split at the material boundaries, where H jumps.
ampere.enclosure.ambiguous: not determined (a current lies in the surface)
ampere.enclosure.on_path: not defined (a current touches the path)
ampere.explain.verified: The numerical circulation of H equals the independently counted free current within the stated tolerance.
ampere.explain.not_converged: The quadrature did not reach the requested accuracy; no comparison is made. Move the path away from sources or loosen the tolerance.
ampere.explain.ambiguous: A current lies in the spanning surface or touches its edge, so the enclosed current is not well defined. The circulation is shown, but not compared.
ampere.explain.intersects_source: The path runs through an ideal current filament, where H is infinite: the circulation is not defined.
ampere.explain.unsupported: The enclosed current cannot be counted for this path with this model (for the ideal toroid only paths coaxial with it are supported). The circulation is shown, but not compared.
ampere.explain.failed: The circulation and the enclosed current differ by more than the tolerance. This indicates a problem and is reported, not hidden.
ampere.explain.invalid: The path is not a valid closed, planar, simple curve.
ampere.about: Only free currents count in ∮H·dl. A permanent magnet has no free current: around it ∮H·dl = 0 even though ∮B·dl ≠ 0, because B also includes the bound current K = M × n. The result does not depend on the path's shape, only on which currents it links.
eq.usage.approximation: Idealized comparison, not the solver's field
probe.mNotConverged: The magnet's surface integral did not reach its tolerance at this point; the value is shown but less accurate.
probe.mStatus.core_boundary: On the surface of the ideal core
probe.mStatusExplain.sheet: The side wall carries the bound surface current K = M × n: the tangential B jumps by μ₀K across it, so B and H have no single value here (within {tol}). The one-sided limits are shown instead.
probe.mStatusExplain.end_face: B is continuous across an end face (no surface current there), but H jumps by M, so H has no single value here (within {tol}).
probe.mStatusExplain.core_boundary: In the ideal model the field drops from its core value to exactly zero at the core surface (within {tol}). The one-sided limits are shown instead.
profile.title: Field along the axis
profile.aria: Axial component of B along the symmetry axis of the selected source
profile.solenoidNote: Solid: B·â of the finite coil, computed by the engine at 161 points on its axis. Dashed: the ideal long-solenoid value μ₀nI over the winding (shaded), an idealization for comparison. The finite coil falls to about half at its ends and has a fringe field beyond them.
profile.magnetNote: B·â of the magnet on its axis, computed by the engine (shaded: the magnet). B is continuous through the end faces; it is largest at the centre and continues outside, where it returns.
legend.magnet: permanent magnet ends (M points from S to N inside)
legend.core: ideal toroid core (linear, μᵣ); field exactly zero outside it
legend.amperePath: Ampère path with its normal; rings: free currents through it (green along n̂, red against, amber undetermined)
legend.bhMagnet: B and H are different quantities. Outside magnets B = μ₀H; inside a magnet H = B/μ₀ − M, so H can point against B.
legend.bhCore: B and H are different quantities. In the ideal core B = μ₀μᵣH; outside it both are zero.
probe.mPrecision: Very close to an ideal filament: float64 arithmetic limits the relative accuracy of B and H here to about {bound}. The value is the true near-filament field, not capped.
ampere.precisionFloor: The path passes so close to a filament that float64 limits the circulation to about ±{floor}, more than the tolerance {tol}: it is therefore not reported as verified.
time.linesPaused: field lines are computed when paused
faraday.title: Faraday's law and magnetic flux
faraday.intro: A stationary measurement surface bounded by a closed planar path. Φ_B = ∫B·n dS is integrated over the surface; the EMF ∮E_ind·dl is integrated independently along its boundary, traversed counter-clockwise about the normal n̂. Faraday's law states ∮E_ind·dl = −dΦ_B/dt. Magnetoquasistatic model; the surfaces are measurement tools, not conductors.
faraday.none: No measurement surface yet. Add one above.
faraday.corner: dI/dt jumps at this instant: the right-hand (after) derivative is used; dΦ/dt and the EMF are not uniquely defined here.
faraday.noChange: No source current changes at this instant: dΦ_B/dt and the EMF are exactly zero.
faraday.trend.increasing: The flux along the positive normal n̂ is increasing (dΦ_B/dt > 0).
faraday.trend.decreasing: The flux along the positive normal n̂ is decreasing (dΦ_B/dt < 0).
faraday.trend.steady: The flux is momentarily not changing (|dΦ_B/dt| below 1e-9 of its maximum).
faraday.circulation.along_path: The EMF is positive: E_ind circulates along the boundary's traversal (counter-clockwise about n̂), opposing the decrease of flux.
faraday.circulation.against_path: The EMF is negative: E_ind circulates against the boundary's traversal (clockwise about n̂), opposing the increase of flux.
faraday.lenzNote: Lenz's law opposes the change of flux, not the flux itself. No conducting circuit is modelled, so no induced current is shown: only E_ind and the EMF.
faraday.mutualNote: M₁₂: flux through this surface per ampere of the source (sign by n̂). M₂₁: flux of this boundary's own 1 A field through the source's turns, computed independently. EMF = −M₁₂ dI/dt. No current flows in the measurement loop.
faraday.about: Φ_B uses each source's magnetic field at 1 A, scaled by its current; dΦ_B/dt uses the analytical dI/dt of each profile. The EMF is the line integral of E_ind = −∂A/∂t (Coulomb-gauge vector potential). Two different fields and quadratures are compared, so their agreement is a real check of Faraday's law. Magnetoquasistatic: the displacement current is neglected; no moving parts (no v × B), no induced currents.
profile.waveform: Current I(t) over the playback range (engine-evaluated); cyan: simulation time; orange dots: corners where dI/dt jumps
profile.typeHint: How the source current depends on time. The signed current keeps its usual direction convention; a negative value reverses it.
profile.rampNote: Before the ramp the start current is held, after it the final current (no extrapolation).
profile.piecewiseNote: Linear between keyframes (strictly increasing times); the first and last values are held outside them.
probe.eIndUnsupported: E_ind is not evaluated: a source without a vector potential (infinite wire or ideal toroid) changes at this time.
probe.eIndNote: E_ind = −∂A/∂t is the induced, nonconservative part of the electric field (Coulomb gauge, magnetoquasistatic). It is not the electrostatic field of charges, which is shown separately, and not a complete electric field.
legend.eInd: E_ind arrows: induced electric field −∂A/∂t (orange, length ∝ log|E_ind|); not the electrostatic E
legend.fluxSurface: Faraday measurement surface with its normal; orange cones: sense of E_ind circulation (Lenz)
legend.forceScale: Force arrows are scaled to the largest force shown; directions are exact.
rod.name: Rod circuit
rod.title: Sliding rod: {name}
rod.intro: Two stationary rails along local x, joined by a fixed segment at x = 0; the rod joins them at x(t) and moves along the rails. Only the rod has a velocity; the rails and the connecting segment are at rest. Ideal thin conductors: no current, resistance or friction is modelled.
motion.title: Motion
motion.intro: The surface and its boundary move rigidly: r(t) = R(t) r_local + c(t), with material velocity u = V + ω × (r − c). The stored position and rotation are the reference pose. The engine evaluates the pose and the velocities at the simulation time.
motion.omegaHint: Signed; right-hand rule about the axis, which passes through the surface's centre.
motion.turnsHint: Only for an explicitly defined coil of N identical, coincident turns in series: every flux and EMF is multiplied by N.
motion.turnsNote: {n} turns in series: flux linkage NΦ and N-fold EMF
motion.conventionHint: Where a conductor's velocity jumps, the instantaneous motional EMF is not uniquely defined; choose a one-sided value to evaluate it.
motion.historyHint: Step or play the simulation time to build the waveform from computed results.
motion.historyNote: {n} computed times; lines join computed points only.
lorentz.title: Test charge
lorentz.intro: A test charge q with its own laboratory-frame velocity v (not a conductor velocity) feels F = q(E + v × B). It does not change the fields. Nonrelativistic.
lorentz.chargeHint: Positive, negative or zero; reversing the sign reverses every force.
lorentz.noWork: F_B is perpendicular to v, so (v × B)·v = 0: the magnetic force changes the direction of motion but never the speed. Only qE·v changes the kinetic energy.
lorentz.trajIntro: Nonrelativistic test-particle motion m dv/dt = q(E + v × B) in the prescribed fields (Boris scheme). No radiation, self-field or particle interactions.
lorentz.toleranceHint: Largest gyration angle ω_c Δt per step, and the largest fraction of the distance to a singular region covered per step.
lorentz.useRange: Use the trajectory time range for playback
lorentz.sampleNote: computed sample at or before t = {t}
lorentz.magneticOnly: Magnetic forces only along the path: the kinetic energy must stay constant.
circ.title: Passive circuits
circ.intro: Closed conductors with resistance and self-inductance, driven only by changing flux (no applied voltage). Their induced currents are solved over the time range, add their own field, and feel electromagnetic forces. Measurement surfaces stay measurement surfaces; convert one explicitly to make it a circuit.
circ.name: Circuit name
circ.tooMany: {n} time steps: at most 2001 samples can be solved; enlarge Δt or shorten the range.
circ.materialHint: Nominal room-temperature conductivity (approximate constant; no temperature dependence).
circ.wireHint: Finite wire radius: needed for the self-inductance (an ideal filament has none) and for R = ℓ/(σπr²).
circ.resistanceHint: Computed from the geometry's length × turns, or a given lumped value.
circ.resistanceRodHint: The sliding-rod circuit needs a given total resistance (its length changes).
circ.inductanceHint: μ₀a[ln(8a/r_w) − 2] for circular loops with r_w/a ≤ 0.1 (approximate); other shapes need a given value.
circ.mechHint: Prescribed: the rod follows its motion profile. Dynamic: m d²x/dt² = F_ext + F_em − b dx/dt, solved with the circuit.
circ.diskApprox: Reduced-order axisymmetric approximation: concentric annular bands, each a circular loop; axisymmetric fields and circular disks only; no skin effect, radial currents, temperature or thermal effects.
circ.bandsHint: Refine to check that the current distribution stabilizes; bands must stay at least half the thickness wide.
circ.recip: Reciprocity M_ij = M_ji: largest relative difference {rel}.
circ.energyPlot: Magnetic energy, Joule heat, kinetic energy
circ.about: The circuit equations L dI/dt = EMF_ext − RI − (dL/dt)I are solved with an implicit adaptive method over the whole time range; transformer and motional EMF are counted once each, the circuit's own (singular) filament field only through its self-inductance. Forces use the field of every other source. Out of scope: applied voltages, networks and capacitors, skin effect, temperature, general 3D eddy currents.
probe.insideConductor: inside the conductor: the filament model does not apply here
probe.passiveRateUnavailable: A moving circuit carries current: ∂B/∂t and E_ind of that contribution are not evaluated.
